summary.name: Graffiti / Street Art. This is a supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection.
summary.visualIdentity: Spray-painted lettering, tags, wall texture and street graphics form one coherent lettering style and palette. Overspray and layered paint are used selectively. Strokes are revealed, areas are overpainted and graphic layers are replaced while the main message stays recognizable.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to lettering-focused pieces. Music promos and event teasers are explicit only as a hybrid with style-105. Culture explainers appear only as a best-for entry for the style-054 flyer-insert hybrid. Motion-037 and motion-038 list this style as compatible. Other topics are inferred.
summary.limitations: The principal message must stay readable through overpaint and strokes. Avoid random overspray, over-layering, photocopy wall noise and mixed palettes. Not every stroke should land on a beat. Source review covers only one frame per second for seconds 1–8, so no verified motion, sub-second timing, audio or later scenes exist.
summary.palette: Background policy is scene_dependent. The status is a style-compatible suggestion for new work when no approved palette is supplied. Direction: selected spray-paint colors on a neutral wall. Example tokens, not mandatory: background #E7E1D4, foreground #272631, accents #BC4861, #388A8B and #CEA248. Choose the background from the scene. Foreground on background measures 11.449:1. Accent_1 and accent_2 text pairings fail 4.5:1 and are decorative only. Gradients are disabled. Approved exact colors override these examples.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit technique: seeded spray brushes and path masks, with paint coverage and stroke movement controlled by time. Tags and main lettering are prepared separately. Smooth authored movement is allowed where it helps, while sharp cuts and reading holds are preserved. Optional references: motion-037 (letter fragments release, phrase steps in) and motion-038 (punctuation zoom), each only if the scene contains that asset. Motion-012 and motion-015 are optional chapter or story patterns. Video state must derive from composition time, not pointer or scroll input.
summary.audio: Unspecified; no audio is required. Style-level direction is task-specific and may include music, voiceover, sound effects, ambience or silence. Music-synced reveals apply only to the style-105 hybrid and need actual audio analysis. No beat or speech timing has been measured. Honor explicit user audio choices and avoid defaulting to a genre.
summary.assetRequirements: No uploads are required. Load local fonts and assets before rendering. Prepare tags and main lettering as separate layers. Inspect glyph or punctuation assets before using motion-037 or motion-038. Exact copy, fonts, duration, aspect ratio and frame rate are unspecified. No source frames were supplied, so do not invent brand marks or copy.
summary.combinations: Graffiti works alone for lettering-focused pieces. Style-105 adds beat-synced spray reveals for music promos; it uses the primary spray palette only and keeps the message readable. Style-054 adds zine flyer cutaways as separate inserts; the wall remains the main scene, and palettes must not mix.
summary.productionApproach: Use HyperFrames by default for scene assembly and export, with data-composition-id, clip timing and one paused GSAP timeline registered in window.__timelines. Canvas 2D and SVG are the style renderers, and GSAP is the motion engine. Motion is optional only with verified seeking. Chroma-js can validate contrast. Use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limit applies, and record the reason.
